A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MaskGaussian research work, with 14 pages including four supplementary pages. Full text and rendered-page inspection support comparison of all sections, equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original rendering experiments, baseline comparisons, and ablations in Section 4 and supplementary Sections 7–10. Table 1 explicitly distinguishes author-run results from externally sourced results.

after.justification: v3 reports the same original MaskGaussian experiments, author-run baseline comparisons, ablations, and per-scene evaluations in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The probabilistic masks, Gumbel-Softmax sampling, masked rasterization, training objective, and pruning procedure are unchanged. The appendix corrections repair the derivation without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same scenes from Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending, retaining the same training-from-scratch, post-training, and extreme-pruning scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including 3DGS, Compact3DGS, RadSplat, RadSplat-Light, LightGaussian, and the Taming-3DGS comparisons.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, training budgets, mask-penalty settings, and testing procedures are identical. This includes the standard 30,000-iteration training and the 5,000-iteration post-training comparison.

E4.justification: Both retain the same sampling, rasterization, and masking-loss ablations, training-dynamics analysis, extreme-pruning comparison, and Gaussian spatial-distribution visualization. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and empirical figures are unchanged, including supplementary Tables 8–13. For example, Table 1 retains MaskGaussian-alpha PSNR values of 27.43, 23.72, and 29.69 across the three datasets.

T1.justification: Supplementary Section 6 replaces both summations in Eq. (13) with products and replaces the summation defining final transmittance in Eq. (16) with a product. These localized mathematical corrections make those steps consistent with the chain rule and transmittance recurrence; the final gradient expression is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about probabilistic pruning, gradients for unsampled Gaussians, rendering quality, compression, and speed.

C2.justification: The explanations of mask gradients, preservation of fine details, pruning-induced regularization, and applicability are unchanged. No substantive limitation or qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: CUDA implementation information, NVIDIA RTX 4090 hardware, hyperparameters, pruning instructions, and the code-access link are unchanged. No technical reproducibility information is added.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, citations, and all 40 reference entries are identical, preserving the same positioning relative to Gaussian pruning and dynamic masking research.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v2 dated 2 Apr 2025 to v3 dated 14 Jun 2025. Prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–13 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. The page layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects erroneous sums to products in supplementary Eqs. (13) and (16), improving the mathematical accuracy and internal consistency of the mask-gradient derivation. This is a limited quality improvement; the method, experimental evidence, and conclusions otherwise remain unchanged.
